gen-dafont-neon-gf-sofia-sans: Neon glows like a sign, every line drawn at a single width. Sofia Sans, a rounded sans-serif with no thick-and-thin swing, would carry paragraphs smoothly, its open-sided letters never tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-stack-sans-headline: Glowing, unbroken lines of constant width make Neon feel lit from within. Stack Sans Headline's monoline skeleton and generous gaps keep small sizes crisp, so the glow above never has to compete.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-ubuntu-sans: Neon buzzes with spacious letter pairs and lines that never thin out. Ubuntu Sans reads like bent copper pipe, big-eyed lowercase and unfinished curves keeping a long block of text lively and contemporary.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-orbit: Digital and futuristic, Neuropol has a single-weight outline feel and letters closed tight. And while Neuropol is best at sealed, outlined shapes, Orbit is best at curves that stop short and characters floating apart.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-aldrich: Neuropolitical pulls words apart letter by letter, each stroke a glowing neon tube of steady width. Aldrich does the opposite job, holding an x-height close to the capitals with round letters that look cupped.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-alexandria: Alexandria keeps a big body with short stems above and below, and its c terminals open wide. Neuropolitical, with its spread-out letters and neon-tube lines, supplies the glow, and Alexandria holds the page together beneath it.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern and unfussy, with crayon-thick lowercase strokes and terminals that point outward like tongs. But the heading's total lack of calligraphic swell on any downstroke is what makes Neuropolitical stand apart from this sturdy body.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-devana: Geometric to the core, Neuropolitical pulls words apart letter by letter, its stroke ends as wide as the middle. Anek Devanagari handles the quieter work with distinctly open letter mouths and a generous middle zone.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-kannad: Anek Kannada lifts its x-height like a squared-off woodblock letter. What stands out most is the gap between Neuropolitical's bent-copper tubular strokes and a body whose terminals stop far from the stem.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-anek-latin: Wired and glowing: Neuropolitical draws each stroke like a cable, one thickness from end to end. While Neuropolitical handles the flash, Anek Latin does the steadier work, with lowercase nearly reaching the capitals and letters held open.
